title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Pinecrest Bank
next_steps: Send updated pricing for Dedicated 2x capacity by 2027-07-09
Share SOC 2 report and network diagrams (VPC peering options)
Schedule benchmark in us-east-1 to validate latency & throughput week of 2027-07-12
Confirm PO / contract extension timeline by 2027-07-15
action_items: Jordan Reyes: send pricing & renewal doc by 2027-07-09
Priya Shah: set up benchmark run and test plan by 2027-07-12
Liam O'Connor: provide current traffic matrix and peak qps by 2027-07-08
Nadia Chen: share security questions and any additional compliance checklist by 2027-07-10

summary: Customer is evaluating a 2x capacity Dedicated upgrade plus adding us-east-1 region and a 12-month contract extension. Security sign-off (SOC2/VPC/KMS) is required; Redwood to run benchmarks and provide updated pricing and network diagrams.
transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-07-06
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Liu (Redwood CSM); Sam Patel (Pinecrest - Head of MLOps), Aisha Gomez (Pinecrest - VP Product), Liam O'Connor (Pinecrest - Infra Manager), Nadia Chen (Pinecrest - Security)

[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in, hope you all got the agenda. we're mainly here to talk renewal and the expansion asks - capacity, another region, and timing. sam, do you want to kick off with current priorities?
[00:22] Sam Patel: yeah thanks Jordan. so, high level, we've seen steady growth - our peak qps for inference is about 650 right now but spikes to ~1.2k during batch closing windows. the current Dedicated node pool is coping but margins are thin. we're looking at a 2x reserved capacity to get headroom and consistent latency. also leadership wants another region, us-east-1, for DR and lower latency for east coast customers.
[00:48] Aisha Gomez: and from product side, we want to expand chat & customer support summarization across more accounts by Q4, so the timeline is kinda compressed. we also want a 12 month extension to lock pricing.
[01:12] Priya Shah: okay that's helpful. when you say 2x, are you referring to GPU count or throughput target? and do you have pref for instance types? (small pause) also curious about burst capacity needs.
[01:28] Liam O'Connor: mostly throughput; we'd probably want the same instance class - the nV-d type you recommended earlier - but tuned. burst is important for end-of-day jobs, maybe temporary autoscale to 3x for short windows.
[01:41] Jordan Reyes: got it. we can propose a Dedicated config that reserves 2x baseline with autoscale for bursts to 3x. we'll include estimated costs. quick note - adding us-east-1 will require provisioning Dedicated pools there; capacity lead time is about 2-3 weeks depending on availability.
[02:05] Nadia Chen: on security, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, network diagrams for VPC peering, KMS/HSM options, and confirmation whether logs are retained in customer-controlled storage. also any data residency concerns - we're fine with us-east-1 but need data never to leave that region for certain workflows.
[02:30] Mark Liu: totally, Nadia. we have a SOC 2 package and we can share network diagrams. KMS integration is supported; you can bring-your-own-key via KMS or HSM connectors. log retention can be configured to ship to your S3 in your account - we'll include options in the doc.
[02:53] Sam Patel: perfect. also can Redwood support warm cache warming across regions? meaning like prefix cache pre-population so cold starts aren't terrible when traffic shifts east?
[03:08] Priya Shah: yes, we do prefix/KV caching and cross-region warming is doable as part of the deployment plan. it'll add some upfront cost for the pre-pop but reduces latency spikes.
[03:25] Aisha Gomez: on pricing, why don't we just lock a flat rate for the 12 months? leadership wants predictability. i'm worried about surprises from autoscale.
[03:41] Jordan Reyes: we can propose a committed reserved capacity price for the baseline 2x, and a capped burst usage rate. think of it like committed + capped overages - that keeps surprises limited but allows flexibility.
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: would the cap be usage-based per token or per-hour of extra GPU? we need to map to our internal cost model.
[04:10] Jordan Reyes: typically we charge burst per GPU-hour and a per-token egress for API calls, but we can present an alternative blended rate for the contract term. i'll note that as an action.
[04:23] [05:00] Sam: there's also the competitor angle - LargeCloudAI pitched managed endpoints with multi-region support, but their token costs were higher and latencies less predictable. we want to validate performance before we move.
[05:20] Priya Shah: understood. that's why we should run a benchmark - Priya can set up a load test that mimics your peak and 2x peak to show latency and p95 numbers across regions.
[05:32] Priya Shah: action: I'll plan a benchmark that runs in us-west-2 and us-east-1; target metrics: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms for your main prompt profile. is that acceptable?
[05:45] Sam Patel: sounds good. p95 of 120 ms would be great. also we want to measure token cost per 1k tokens across workloads.
[05:56] Aisha Gomez: quick Q - are there any model variants that Redwood recommends for lower cost? quantized variants or smaller models for routine responses?
[06:10] Priya Shah: yes, we can recommend quantized variants and mixing models: use a smaller quantized model for routine summarization, route higher-quality generation to a larger model. Redwood Optimize provides recommendations per prompt set.
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: for the us-east-1 pool, what's the lead time? you said 2-3 weeks - is that guaranteed?
[06:33] Jordan Reyes: depends on available Dedicated capacity in the target region; for planning we estimate 2-3 weeks after contract sign. if you need faster, we can start with hosted burst in us-east-1 temporarily but that has different SLA and data flow considerations.
[06:50] Nadia Chen: hosted burst introduces data egress risks; we need to confirm encryption in transit and at rest, and that routing doesn't send PII outside region. can you get legal to confirm that?
[07:04] Mark Liu: yes, we'll include the data flow diagram and encryption details. our hosted vs dedicated parity ensures TLS in transit and KMS-managed keys at rest, but we'll flag the hosted burst caveat.
[07:18] Sam Patel: timeline-wise, we need to have pricing and security docs by next week so leadership can sign the PO mid-July.
[07:28] Jordan Reyes: ok next steps - we'll send an updated pricing deck with committed 2x plus capped overages, SOC 2 and network diagrams, and a benchmark plan. priya will schedule the tests for week of July 12. does that align?
[07:45] Aisha Gomez: yes. also want to confirm the contract extension - we're looking at 12 months with the option to scale capacity mid-term.
[07:55] Jordan Reyes: that's fine; we can include scalable clauses and a simple amendment process. we'll draft language for mid-term capacity increases and pricing tiers.
[08:06] [10:00] Sam: on the benchmarks, please include the specific prompt sets: ticket summarization, chat multi-turn, and fraud detection rerank. those are the main ones causing spikes.
[08:24] Priya Shah: got it. please share the prompt examples and sample payloads - that will help reproduce realistic latency and token counts. can you upload them to the benchmark spreadsheet you shared earlier?
[08:36] Sam Patel: yeah i'll add them by EOD. liam will also export the qps curve and traffic matrix.
[08:44] Liam O'Connor: i'll do that. one more infra note - our team prefers VPC peering to a private endpoint rather than open internet egress. any special steps?
[08:55] Mark Liu: VPC peering is supported; we'll map the steps and include the peering CIDR recommendations. there may be firewall rules and route table edits on your side.
[09:08] Nadia Chen: and on audit logs - can logs be shipped to our SIEM in real-time or near real-time? we need retention of 3 years for certain logs.
[09:22] Mark Liu: logs can be shipped to your S3 and then your SIEM; retention policies can be configured to meet 3-year requirements. there are costs for long-term storage, we'll call that out.
[09:36] Jordan Reyes: ok i'm going to recap actions - Jordan to send pricing and renewal doc by Friday 7/9, Priya to run benchmarks week of 7/12, Liam to share traffic matrix by 7/8, Nadia to provide security checklist by 7/10, Aisha to confirm budget & regions by 7/11. anything missing?
[09:58] Aisha Gomez: can you include estimated token/unit costs for the blended rate? leadership wants that in the deck.
[10:06] Jordan Reyes: yes, we'll include blended per-token and per-GPU-hour numbers and examples for monthly estimates.
[10:12] Sam Patel: also include an estimated migration plan for cross-region cache warm up - what's the downtime or performance impact during cutover?
[10:24] Priya Shah: minimal; we'll schedule a warm-up window and pre-populate caches, expect short tail latency increases for 15-30 minutes during cutover for cold keys.
[10:40] Liam O'Connor: one more technical deep dive request - can Priya's team provide details on kernel-optimizations and quantization profiles used for the model variants? our infra folks want to see CPU/GPU utilization numbers.
[10:56] Priya Shah: yes we can add a short tech appendix about compilation, kernel selection, and quantization tradeoffs; we'll include utilization estimates based on your prompt profile.
[11:10] Jordan Reyes: great. any blockers on the legal side from your side that we should know before sending the docs?
[11:20] Nadia Chen: standard NDAs are fine; we may have a few clauses around data processing addendum for regulated customers - i'll mark them in the checklist.
[11:32] Mark Liu: we'll also add a one-page runbook for failover to the east region and rollback steps.
[11:42] Jordan Reyes: perfect. if there are no more questions, let's wrap. thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark.
[11:52] Aisha Gomez: thanks all.
[12:00] Meeting ended

Notes on transcript: transcription may mis-hear some product names (e.g., "nV-d" for NVidia instance families) and occasional timestamps are approximate. There was light crosstalk between Sam and Aisha near the section on pricing.
